body.text: Sat, 15 Aug, 11:00 pm, Final score, AUS 198 & 284, BAN 426 & 1/57
South Africa–Australia first Test live updates: Matt Renshaw notches Durban century
Matt Renshaw's first Test century since January 2017 sees Australia's rearguard action continue on day two of the first Test against South Africa.
Australia lost just two lower-order wickets during an extended first session in Durban, piling on 90 runs to reach lunch at 8-277.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, keep up with all the stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio call on the ABC Listen app.

133rd - Renshaw hunting his highest Test score
That single to end the last over took Renshaw to 181 off 370. His highest Test score is 184.
132nd over - Anrich Nortje resumes to Matt Renshaw
Will Renshaw try to attack a bit, or is he focused on trying to make it to 200? And getting Australia to 400?
Beaten on the outside edge. Anrich Nortje has bowled a few of them, and keeps coming back for more. Credit where it's due.
But there have been A LOT of leaves by the Aussies. How many balls would've hit the stumps from the South African seamers today? Not many I'd wager.
BANG! Short and crushed on the hook by Renshaw with a gorgeous stroke for four. Perfectly played by a tall man.
And he gets the luck as a thick edge flies too fine for the lone slip in place. But hey, he's the reason the field is so spread. The epitome of 'you make your own luck'.
131st over - Marco Jansen to pepper Josh Hazlewood
He's very much a number 11, so I expect Jansen to get him here, stranding Matt Renshaw on a paltry 175.
Oh no. Jansen keeps the short ball tactics to Hazlewood, who's able to run a ball down to third man and steal a single to get off strike.
Aggravation for Jansen as he fires in the yorker and Renshaw drops a bat on it, getting a thick edge away to point for a single.
Hazlewood has two balls to face, and ducks under a bouncer on the first.
Jansen goes full, and Hazlewood manages to keep it out.
130th over - Hazlewood is getting checked out
He's OK after copping a blow to the helmet, so Matt Renshaw will face Anrich Nortje.
There's a hook shot from Renshaw, well controlled down to the ground to deep backward square. They don't take the single off the second ball.
Expert short leg fielding by David Bedingham to keep Renshaw on strike as he works off his hip.
SIX! Nortje bangs in a bouncer to end the over in an attempt to keep Renshaw from retaining the strike. He succeeds in one respect, but he does concede a maximum off Renshaw's uppercut.
129th over - Marco Jansen wants to finish this now
He barely appealed and barely smiled after finally getting Lyon out. He's had enough of this.
He's around the wicket and bangs in the bouncer, which collects Josh Hazlewood on the body.
GOT HIM! Nathan Lyon is out LBW at long last
Marco Jansen spears in a full one from around the wicket and smashes into Nathan Lyon's pads as he plays back.
He's stone dead LBW and Chris Gaffaney says as much. Lyon reviews, but immediately walks off before the replays confirm his incredible outness.
He goes for 27 and the partnership with Renshaw ends on a massive 134, the second most by any Aussie ninth-wicket pair.
129th over - More frustration for South Africa

Marco Jansen bangs in from back of a length and Lyon tries to work off his hip to the leg side. He gets a massive edge, but the ball just balloons over the slips. Not only is it not caught, not only is it a run conceded, but now Lyon is off strike.
They like their chances against Renshaw with the short ball, and that's what Jansen sets the field for.
He looks ungainly as he tries to lean back and uppercut a short one.

Good grief, they might be onto something here. Renshaw defends bizarrely inside out and pops a ball up to short point, but it falls safely. Dumb luck really and he takes the single with three balls left.
128th over - Nortje steams in again
He bangs in a bouncer and Renshaw rides it calmly. Same goes for the full one as Renshaw props forward to defend.
Renshaw is in no rush whatsoever. Interesting to me that he isn't even considering a hook or pull to the short stuff. There's risk involved obviously.
Well bowled and well negotiated by Renshaw, who gets his gloves down and out of the way of a bouncer.
127th over - Marco Jansen is back too
So this is a big moment in this match. Bavuma clearly feels he needs to break this partnership now, and he's bringing his strike men back.
There's a big appeal from Kyle Verreynne for a catch down the leg side, but no-one else seems all that interested. It doesn't look close to anything, and as such there's no support for a review.
SHOT! Short and hooked away for four by Nathan Lyon.
Jansen tries a new angle from around the wicket into Lyon, who's fishing outside off. This looks a more threatening line from the left-armer.
And Lyon ends the over with a full-blooded cover drive that hits nothing but air. It'll make a great photo, so long as the ball isn't anywhere in the frame. Good shapes.
126th over - Anrich Nortje comes on to bowl
A big change for South Africa with the speedster returning as Lyon is forced into the strike.
But he expertly whips off his thigh to deep backward square leg and takes a single off the second ball. Disappointing for Nortje, Bavuma and the Proteas.
Bavuma and Nortje are having a long chat on the penultimate delivery about how to keep Renshaw on strike to end the over.
Renshaw is unfazed and happily defends the last two balls of the over.
125th over - "BORING AUSTRALIA"

That's the cry from the crowd, and they're not wrong, but it's what the game calls for. We're still before tea on day two of this Test. Matt Renshaw has a double century in the offing. He can put miles in the legs of the South African bowlers early in this series. Why not take his time?
Keshav Maharaj continues and Renshaw can't find the gaps.
Temba Bavuma tries some thing new with a close catching mid-on. That at least stops Renshaw from just bunting an easy single down the ground to long-on.
Now, with one ball left, the South Africans bring the field up.
WHACK! Renshaw smacks four down the ground. Runs for Australia, a bit of excitement for the fans and Nathan Lyon will have to be on strike to start the next over. Everyone, except Lyon, wins.
124th over - Renshaw dancing away

After a little shimmy in between overs to Shakira's Waka Waka, Renners is dancing down the pitch to Markram and clipping down the ground. But he's not taking early singles. The field is spread, daring the centurion to take on the field and force the issue. Instead he just waits until the fourth ball and clips to long-on for a single.
And again Lyon takes the last two balls without any trouble.
123rd over - Maharaj vs Matt

There's a lot of turn into Renshaw here, who's getting across and trying to work to the leg side. He's not having much luck, so he knocks another one down the ground to long-on, takes the single and gives Lyon two balls to face.
And again the number 10 is equal to the task.
122nd over - More from Markram
Renshaw is happy to defend three or four, knock a single and come back next over.
And that's exactly what he does to long-on.
Lyon to face one ball … and he defends with a stony bat.
121st over - The crowd is getting rowdy
The ambience mics at Kingsmead are picking up a few audience members cheering and getting up and about with raucous applause and cheers akin to a "Mashed potatoes!" golf shout.
Four! Clattered to the rope by Renshaw wide of mid-off.
Another well worked single gives Lyon one ball to face and he's almost undone by a glorious delivery that rips past the outside edge.
120th over - Aiden Markram is getting a go
The opening batter bowling his offies is not usually a sign of a bowling team in total control.
Renshaw slaps one straight to Temba Bavuma at cover and the crowd goes up for a classic crowd catch.
There appears to be a bit more aggression from Renshaw here, but he's not getting silly with it.
119th over - Renshaw dealing with Maharaj
He looks really comfortable against the left-arm spinner.
Four! A big reach on the reverse paddle sweep and Renshaw clips a full toss to the rope behind point.
Temba Bavuma blocks off the reverse sweep, so Renshaw goes conventional and helps himself to a single to retain the strike for the next over. Expertly done.
Key Event
150 for Matt Renshaw!
The Aussie star removes his helmet for an understated celebration after reverse sweeping for another boundary and that's his second 150 in Tests.
What a knock this has been.
119th over - Keshav Maharaj takes up the spin mantle
Matt Renshaw on strike and reverse sweeping.
